correctness.rationale: The theorem fixes the nonnilpotent bracket [h,e]=e and central rank r. Every subalgebra is classified by ideal subspaces, e-containing lifts, or graphs C(U,c,w); B-C and C-C nonpermuting criteria give mutually exhaustive disjoint cases. The Gaussian subspace-incidence factor W_{u,v,t} counts ordered U,V with intersection dimension t, yielding T_r and N_r without overcounting. The dominant exponent 1+(u+1)(r-u) has one maximizing rank for odd r and two for even r, and generic complementarity yields respectively limit 0 or 1/4 for fixed r. Direct independently written GF(2) enumeration counted all 374 vector subspaces at r=3 and verified 220 Lie subalgebras and 6636 nonpermuting ordered pairs; an independent finite-sum evaluator reproduced r=3,q=2 and numerically approached the parity limit for r=3..8 at q=1009. These finite checks do not establish arbitrary r or q; the analytic classification does.
residual_risks: Fixed central rank r as q grows; no joint r,q growth.
Only aff_1(F_q)⊕F_q^r, not arbitrary solvable or nilpotent Lie algebras.

originality.rationale: The main 2026-09-16 primary paper introduces this permutability probability and calculates Heisenberg/sl2 cases, not a centrally stabilized nonnilpotent affine family. The 2026-10-13 full-rank Heisenberg stabilization result has an analogous parity phenomenon but is based on a two-step nilpotent Lie bracket with central derived ideal, whereas the present [h,e]=e derived ideal is noncentral. Neither same dimensions nor swapping parity indices implies these T,N formulas. Existing dimension-three/four low-rank results are expressly excluded from novelty. No actually inspected source establishes the all-r affine T,N formula or rank parity law; residual risk of an older unindexed affine-subalgebra lattice formula remains.
residual_risks: Older unindexed formulas for solvable two-generator affine Lie algebras with arbitrary abelian central summands may imply the result.
